exposure: minor blood group incompatibility (C, c, E, E+c, Kell)
outcome: clinical course (age of diagnosing jaundice, rebound elevation of serum bilirubin)
responses to treatment (requirement of intravenous immunoglobulin, exchange-erythrocyte transfusions, rehospitalisation for phototherapy)
cohort: Three hundred fifty-five infants hospitalised with the diagnosis of unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia (UHB) were included.
finding: Infants with minor blood group incompatibility had a significantly higher mean age of diagnosing jaundice, lower mean haemoglobin and haematocrit levels at admission, remarkably high rebound elevation of serum bilirubin, and a higher requirement for intravenous immunoglobulin, exchange-erythrocyte transfusions, and rehospitalisation for phototherapy compared to other incompatibility groups.
